question.text:
The coordinates of the foot perpendicular from the point $(1,0,0)$ to the line
$$
\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+1}{-3}=\frac{z+10}{8} \text { are }
$$

solution.text:
Let the equation of $A B$ is $$ \frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-(-1)}{-3}=\frac{z-(-10)}{8}=k $$ Let $L$ be the foot of the perpendicular drawn form $P(1,0,0)$.
$\therefore \quad L=(2 k+1,-3 \mathrm{k}-1,8 k-10)$. Now, direction ratio of $P L=(2 k,-3 k-1,8$ $-10)$ and direction ratio of $A B=(2,-3,8)$ Since, $P L$ is perpendicular to $A B$ $$ \therefore \quad 2(2 k)-3(-3 k-1)+8(8 k-10)=0 $$ Now, $k=\frac{2(1-1)+(-3)(0+1)+8(0+10)}{(2)^2+(-3)^2+(8)^2}$ $$ =\frac{0-3+80}{4+9+64}=\frac{77}{77}=1 $$ $\therefore \quad$ Required co-ordinate $$ =L=(2+1,-3-1,8-10)=(3,-4,-2) \text {. } $$
